answer: Each agent posts a small time-locked deposit when it joins the economy, like planting a cedar: slow to grow, hard to fake. During each honest epoch it earns reputation credits; at epoch end its stake is refunded with interest, so honesty pays. A sybil attacker must forge thousands of distinct identities, each freezing its own deposit for the full epoch, tying up capital that only returns after the reef of honest activity is completed. Sustaining fakes therefore costs more than any payoff, collapsing the attack economically.
